look_here_first: LOOK AT GROWTH HABIT + THE NODES, NOT JUST THE COMMON NAME. Euphorbia villifera generally has ascending/upright branches rather than a flat, rooted mat. At opposite-leaf nodes, its stipules are DISTINCT, THREADLIKE (filiform), unlike E. serpens' fused broad triangular scales. Leaf/stem surfaces are PAPILLATE under strong magnification; most specimens are LONG-HAIRED but completely glabrous forms occur. Most useful reproductive confirmation: SMOOTH THREE-LOBED capsule whose cocci may be elongated into an internally EMPTY tip, which needs DISSECTION to prove. Current public photos show hair, a leaf node, developing capsule and styles but do NOT prove the exact stipule identity, cellular papillae, dissected empty tip or mature seed sculpture. Hays inclusion remains PROVISIONAL and native metrics excluded.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia section Anisophyllum (legacy Chamaesyce). Opposite asymmetric leaves, tiny cyathia rather than normal flowers, and dry 3-lobed capsules.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual or perennial herb with slender taproot or sometimes thickened woody rootstock; stems usually erect to ascending, rarely prostrate/decumbent, about 10–30 cm.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Papillate; usually villous but sometimes glabrous. Hair presence alone is therefore not absolute.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite; blades ovate, about 3–12 × 2–10 mm, base asymmetric and rounded to slightly cordate, margins entire or serrulate, surfaces usually villous but sometimes glabrous; leaf surfaces are papillate.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Distinct, filiform, usually undivided, rarely split into 2–3 segments, about 0.3–0.7 mm; this differs strongly from the fused deltate stipule scale of E. serpens.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Cyathia solitary at distal nodes; 4 pink glands, oval/oblong/trapezoidal, with white-to-pink appendages.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsule oblate-deltoid, about 1.5–2 × 2.1–3.1 mm, glabrous; cocci are often elongated and terminate in an empty distal portion.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds gray-brown to red-brown, ovoid-oblong, weakly 4-angled, about 1–1.4 × 0.6–0.8 mm; smooth, faintly rugose, or with inconspicuous transverse ridges.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Usually upright/ascending branches, about 10–30 cm tall; rare prostrate plants possible. Distinctive relative to typical prostrate sandmat trio but not alone decisive.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Opposite ovate leaves about 3–12 mm long with asymmetric base, sometimes soft-hairy and sometimes essentially glabrous.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stipules distinctly separate, narrow, FILIFORM and small (about 0.3–0.7 mm): inspect with loupe at BOTH sides of leaf node; existing closeup doesn't independently resolve them from hairs.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf blades and stems PAPILLATE under magnification. Surface texture in photos is NOT proof of individual papillae.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Long soft VILLOUS hairs frequently present on foliage and stems but some forms can be glabrous; don't decide from hair density alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small pink cyathial glands with white-pink appendages; capsule smooth/glabrous and approximately 1.5–2 by 2.1–3.1 mm.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. serpens: villifera is usually erect/ascending, has distinct filiform stipules and papillate surfaces; serpens is a glabrous prostrate mat that roots at nodes and has fused deltate stipule scales. Against E. prostrata: villifera has filiform stipules and glabrous capsules with often empty-tipped elongated cocci; prostrata does not root at nodes, has upper-free/lower-fused stipules, and has crisped-villous capsule keels.
